title: Cacao Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Cacao Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Cacao nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in kakaw, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Cacao nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your kakaw (cacao) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, zinc, magnesium, boron, calcium, iron and sulfur. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Cacao seedlings in pots with yellowing leaves (nitrogen shortage), some with brown leaf edges (potassium)

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But zinc, boron, calcium, iron and sulfur stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which cacao nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.
Cacao nutrient deficiency signs, old leaves and young leaves
Shows first on the old leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the old leaves of kakaw
rows: the whole plant, old, lower leaves
Small, evenly soft yellow green leaves on a slow tree. New leaves come out almost white.
old, lower leaves, leaf edges and tips
Old leaves blotchy pale between the veins, then die back from the tip with a sharp edge. New leaves small and narrow.
old, lower leaves, leaf edges and tips
Old leaves get reddish yellow patches between the side veins that die from the tip and edge, with a wavy yellow border.
old, lower leaves, between the veins
Old leaves get tiny black pinpoints with yellow halos between the veins, then a marbled dead edge.

blocks.text: Shows first on the young leaves

blocks.caption: Deficiencies that start on the young leaves of kakaw
rows: young leaves and the tip, between the veins
Sickle leaf: new leaves narrow, curved and lopsided, with wavy edges and pale bands between prominent veins.
young leaves and the tip, fruit, grain or tubers
Many chupons, new leaves twisted and falling before they harden, brittle old leaves with dead tips.
young leaves and the tip, leaf edges and tips
Small yellow green leaves with tiny white spots seen against the light, and dead tips and edges.
young leaves and the tip, between the veins
Leaves dull yellow green with sharp green veins and a bumpy surface between them.
young leaves and the tip, the whole plant
The newest mature leaves evenly yellow green on a very short last flush.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a cacao nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest cacao nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in cacao

blocks.alt: Cacao seedlings in pots with yellowing leaves (nitrogen shortage), some with brown leaf edges (potassium)
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson, CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Growth slows and the leaves harden early, so they stay small. Full grown leaves turn an even soft yellow green, and the oldest leaves of each flush die back from the tip. New leaves come out yellow to almost white. Internodes are short and the leaf stalks stand at a sharp angle to the stem. Fewer flushes mean fewer flowers and pods. You see it most at this stage: young trees in the first years after planting, bearing trees that get no fertilizer, and trees grown without shade. BPI notes nitrogen is most needed at the start of the rainy season and three months later.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in kakaw

Trees that get little or no fertilizer, cacao grown in full sun (BPI notes that proper shade lowers the nutrient need), low organic matter, and leaching rains. In a leaf survey of 63 cocoa farms in Papua New Guinea, a nearby growing area with similar smallholder farming, 95 percent of farms were below the critical nitrogen level.
How to tell it apart

Vascular streak dieback also yellows leaves, but it shows scattered green spots on a yellow leaf on one or two leaves about a meter behind the shoot tip, the leaves drop. Three small dark dots show in the leaf scar with a brown streak inside the twig. To be sure, leaf test: take the second or third leaf of the last flush that is just maturing, four or five leaves from around the canopy of at least 10 trees, skipping damaged leaves, as Yara advises. A soil test for organic matter helps.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency

Apply Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or Urea 46 0 0 in a ring under the canopy after weeding, in two splits at the start and end of the rainy season. The PCA Davao technology guide puts a mature planting of 1,241 trees per hectare yielding 1 tonne of dry beans at about 108 grams of Ammonium sulfate per tree per year. TNAU gives much more, 100 grams of nitrogen per tree per year, doubled for trees bearing over 50 pods. Use the soil and leaf test to choose.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, fertilize every year in splits, mulch with prunings and composted pod husks.
Phosphorus deficiency in cacao

Growth slows early. New leaves keep a normal color but come out smaller and narrower. Older leaves of the previous flush lose color between the veins in blotches, then die from the tip toward the base, with a sharp line between dead and living tissue. Some leaves turn greyish purple before the dead patch forms. Badly hit leaves fall, and flowering and pod setting drop. You see it most at this stage: young trees after planting, and bearing trees at the start of the rainy season, when BPI says phosphorus is most needed for flowering.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in kakaw
Acid soils low in organic matter. A study of eight cacao farms in Davao de Oro found phosphorus generally deficient, on moderately to slightly acid soils with low organic matter.
How to tell it apart

Potassium deficiency starts the same way, but at the advanced stage the dead patch has a wavy, zigzag yellow border instead of a sharp edge. Magnesium deficiency shows small blackish pinpoints with yellow halos first. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH, and a leaf test of the second or third leaf of the last maturing flush.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency

Apply a phosphorus fertilizer in the ring under the canopy, following the soil test. The PCA Davao guide gives about 49 grams of Solophos superphosphate per mature tree per year for a 1 tonne per hectare crop. Complete 14 14 14 for young trees. Yara notes that on low phosphorus soils, rates up to 200 kg P2O5 per hectare raised yields. That the response is best when nitrogen is also enough.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, put phosphorus in the planting hole, add compost or composted pod husks every year, and lime very acid soils.
Potassium deficiency in cacao

blocks.alt: Cacao seedlings whose older leaves have brown, scorched edges from potassium shortage
blocks.caption: Photo: Scot Nelson, CC0 1.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Older leaves show it first. A dull reddish yellow color runs along the midrib, wider at the base, or larger reddish yellow patches form between the side veins near the edge. The patches join and die, usually starting at the tip and edge, and the dead part has a wavy, zigzag yellow border. Leaves fall early. New leaves come out long and narrow. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees under heavy pod loads. BPI says potash is most needed before flowering and while pods grow.
Why potassium deficiency happens in kakaw

Every harvest carries potash away, mostly in the pod husks: the PCA Davao guide counts about 72 kg of potassium removed per tonne of dry beans, 63 kg of it in the husks. Sandy, leached soils and husks that are never returned bring it on.
How to tell it apart

Phosphorus deficiency looks the same at first, but its dead patches have a sharp edge. Magnesium deficiency begins with blackish pinpoints between the veins. To be sure, leaf test of the second or third leaf of the last maturing flush, from at least 10 trees, plus a soil test for potash, calcium and magnesium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 in the ring in two splits. The PCA Davao guide gives about 86 grams per mature tree per year for a 1 tonne per hectare crop. Yara puts 70 to 100 kg K2O per hectare as enough for yields under 1 tonne of beans. TNAU gives 140 grams of K2O per tree per year, doubled for trees bearing over 50 pods.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, return composted pod husks to the trees, give potash every year in splits, and keep potash and magnesium in balance.
Zinc deficiency in cacao

On young leaves the small veins stand out sharply and the tissue between them is pale, which is easy to see against the light. Leaves grow long and narrow with wavy, fluted edges and may twist. Many show a waist near the base or grow more on one side of the midrib, so they curve like a sickle. In bad cases leaves stay tiny, internodes shorten into rosettes, leaves fall early and shoot tips die back, with many small side twigs. You see it most at this stage: young trees in the field and new flushes, often after a drought.
Why zinc deficiency happens in kakaw
Old, leached, sandy soils low in zinc, high pH, heavy phosphate. Roots damaged by drought or waterlogging, which take up less zinc.
How to tell it apart

Boron deficiency can also give sickle leaves. But it also brings brittle leaves with dead tips, a dying top and cracks on the trunk. To be sure, leaf test of the second or third leaf of the last maturing flush. Spray zinc on a few trees: leaves that have already hardened stay misshapen, but the next flush comes out normal.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

TNAU gives a foliar spray of Zinc sulfate at 0.3 to 0.5 percent (3 to 5 grams per liter) every two weeks, three times. In a field trial in New Guinea, young trees sprayed with zinc sulfate every ten days had almost fully recovered after seven months, while unsprayed trees stayed sick.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, avoid overliming and heavy phosphate, mulch to protect roots in the dry season, and include zinc where leaf tests run low.
Magnesium deficiency in cacao

Older leaves first show a faint yellowing between the side veins with small blackish pinpoints. Yellow spots form around the pinpoints, join toward the tip and edge, and the tissue dies, giving a blotchy, marbled leaf. A bright yellow zone borders the dead parts. In bad cases the dead tissue turns almost white with the green veins standing out like ribs, and leaves fall early. You see it most at this stage: bearing trees, after years of potash without magnesium. BPI lists calcium and magnesium as most needed at the start of the rainy season.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in kakaw
Acid, leached soils and heavy potash. In the Papua New Guinea survey most farms had enough magnesium, but in one province 64 percent were short.
How to tell it apart

Potassium deficiency also kills old leaf edges, but without the black pinpoints, and with a wavy yellow border. Calcium deficiency shows white spots, seen against the light, on the newest full grown leaves. To be sure, leaf test of the second or third leaf of the last maturing flush. A soil test for magnesium, potash and calcium together.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

TNAU gives Dolomite at 100 grams per tree per year from the third year after planting. The PCA Davao guide uses about 40 grams of Dolomite per mature tree for a 1 tonne per hectare crop. Where soil pH is fine, use Magnesium sulfate or Kieserite, following the soil test. Do not put magnesium and potash down on the same day.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime with Dolomite instead of plain lime and keep potash and magnesium in balance.
Boron deficiency in cacao

Early signs are many chupons (water shoots) and a few curled leaves. New leaves come out pale, twisted and bent backward, harden while still small and often fall before they mature. Some curve into a sickle. Older leaves turn brittle and rough with dead tips, the most typical sign. The tip bud and then side shoots die so the tree turns bushy, and the trunk and branches may crack and bleed. Flower cushions swell, and pods can be misshapen with brown streaks inside. You see it most at this stage: new flushes and flowering, often after a dry spell.
Why boron deficiency happens in kakaw
Drought and shallow roots. U.S.
How to tell it apart

Zinc deficiency also gives sickle leaves, but without brittle dead tipped leaves, a dying top or trunk cracks. Sucking bugs can also deform pods, so check the leaves and shoots too. To be sure, leaf test of the second or third leaf of the last maturing flush, and a soil test for boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency

No cacao particular rate was found in the sources. Yara notes that boron applied with calcium helps flower set and cuts pod drop. Spray Solubor or apply Borax to the soil at the label rate, then retest. Boron is toxic in excess.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, mulch and keep the soil moist in the dry season.
Calcium deficiency in cacao

Growth nearly stops and leaves stay small and strong yellow green. Full grown leaves of the last flush show many small white spots near the tip and edge when held against the light, and the tip dies. The spots turn reddish yellow, join, and the tip and edge die further, sometimes leaving an oak leaf shape of green tissue. TNAU also notes dead patches near the edge that join into a dead margin on older leaves. You see it most at this stage: young trees on acid soils. BPI lists calcium and magnesium as most needed at the start of the rainy season.
Why calcium deficiency happens in kakaw
Acid, leached soils and heavy potash. Most cacao soils in the Davao de Oro study were moderately to slightly acid, below pH 6.5.
How to tell it apart

Magnesium deficiency also kills leaf edges, but it starts with blackish pinpoints on older leaves. Potassium deficiency gives reddish yellow patches with a wavy border. To be sure, soil test for pH and calcium, and a leaf test of the second or third leaf of the last maturing flush.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

TNAU gives Dolomite at 100 grams per tree per year from the third year. On very acid soils apply Agricultural lime or Dolomite following the soil test. On soils that are not acid use Gypsum. Superphosphate in the PCA program also supplies calcium.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils based on a soil test and keep potash in balance.
Iron deficiency in cacao

Leaves turn a dull yellow green while the veins stay green and sharply outlined. The blade between the side veins bulges up, so the leaf looks bumpy, and the edge can look slightly toothed. TNAU describes it on young leaves, which turn pale yellow, with stunted growth. You see it most at this stage: young trees and new flushes, mostly on wet or limed spots.
Why iron deficiency happens in kakaw
High pH or overlimed soils and waterlogged soils. A leaf survey in Papua New Guinea found 89 percent of farms below the critical iron level.
How to tell it apart

Zinc deficiency also gives a bumpy leaf, but much stronger, and leaves are narrow, waisted or sickle shaped. Nitrogen deficiency yellows the whole leaf including the veins. To be sure, soil test for pH and check drainage. Since leaf iron numbers are hard to read, a test spray of ferrous sulfate on a few trees is the best check.
What to apply for iron deficiency
TNAU gives a foliar spray of Ferrous sulfate at 0.5 percent (5 grams per liter) every two weeks. Fix drainage and stop liming where pH is high.

Sold here with iron: **Ferrous Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Cleveland Industries Inc. (20 percent iron), **Ferrous Sulfate Monohydrate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (30 percent iron), **Grow More Liquid Chelate Iron with Sulfur** by Sagrex Corporation (5 percent iron and 3 percent sulfur) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [iron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/iron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, drain wet spots and do not overlime.
Sulfur deficiency in cacao

It comes on slowly. The last three mature leaves turn evenly yellow green and the internode of the last flush stays very short. Older leaves look patchy from yellowing between the veins, and some yellow at the tip or edge. No field description from cacao farms was found, so this follows a pot trial. You see it most at this stage: young trees, after a long time without any sulfur source.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in kakaw
Soils low in organic matter and fertilizer programs that use only urea and muriate of potash.
How to tell it apart

Nitrogen deficiency also yellows leaves evenly, but it hits the whole tree and the old leaves die back from the tip. Iron deficiency keeps the veins sharply green. To be sure, leaf test of the second or third leaf of the last maturing flush for sulfur. Trees that green up after ammonium sulfate confirm it.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency
Use Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 as the nitrogen source, as the PCA Davao program does, or add Gypsum, following the soil test.

Sold here with sulfur: **Farmfix Sulfur** by Philippine FarmFix, Inc. (99 percent sulfur), **VSI Sulfur Powder** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (99.5 percent sulfur), **Atlas Ammosul** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur) and **Philphos 21 0 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 (ammonium sulfate)). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep a sulfur source in the yearly program and build organic matter.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any cacao nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your kakaw needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Cacao nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my kakaw leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: small, evenly soft yellow green leaves on a slow tree. New leaves come out almost white. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in cacao?
items.a: Apply Ammonium sulfate 21 0 0 or Urea 46 0 0 in a ring under the canopy after weeding, in two splits at the start and end of the rainy season. The PCA Davao technology guide puts a mature planting of 1,241 trees per hectare yielding 1 tonne of dry beans at about 108 grams of Ammonium sulfate per tree per year.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in cacao?
items.a: Apply a phosphorus fertilizer in the ring under the canopy, following the soil test. The PCA Davao guide gives about 49 grams of Solophos superphosphate per mature tree per year for a 1 tonne per hectare crop.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in cacao?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 in the ring in two splits. The PCA Davao guide gives about 86 grams per mature tree per year for a 1 tonne per hectare crop.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my kakaw lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the cacao nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
